short: He turned the Conservatives into a party of empire and working-class votes.
full:
Benjamin Disraeli, a novelist and the only British prime minister of Jewish birth, led a minority government for ten months in 1868 and a majority one from 1874 to 1880. As chancellor he had already carried the Second Reform Act of 1867, roughly doubling the electorate and enfranchising urban working men, on the calculation that they would repay the favour at the polls.

His second ministry passed public health, housing and trade union legislation, but he is remembered for foreign policy. He bought the Khedive of Egypt's Suez Canal shares in 1875 with money borrowed from Rothschild, had Victoria proclaimed Empress of India in 1876, and returned from the Congress of Berlin in 1878 claiming peace with honour after checking Russian expansion in the Balkans. Costly wars in Afghanistan and Zululand, and an agricultural depression, lost him the 1880 election. He died the following year.
